prompt.context: A private equity client owns a specialized pharma manufacturer called OncoCo which focuses on cancer treatments. OncoCo is not only profitable, but also experienced steady growth in the past years. Hence, the PE fund was surprised when the management board of OncoCo stated that they expect declining profits in the future. OncoCo's management board has also suggested, to cushion the decline with the acquisition of an additional asset. In particular, OncoCo's board received the opportunity to purchase the commercial rights of liquid morphine.
prompt.question: The PE fund has asked us to figure out why a decline is expected and whether they should move forward with the acquisition of the commercial rights of liquid morphine.

clarifying_info.q: What is the PE fund's target EBITDA margin?
What is liquid morphine used for?
clarifying_info.a: Used to treat severe pain, for example after an operation or a serious injury, or pain from cancer or a heart attack. It is fast acting and used for pain which is expected to last for a short time. Usually prescribed by pain specialists.

clarifying_info.q: What does acquiring the commercial rights mean?
clarifying_info.a: OncoCo will be able to produce and sell the product under its name. Often pharma companies purchase existing stocks and have the opportunity to either renegotiate the contracts with raw material suppliers or continue under existing conditions.

clarifying_info.q: How much is the revenue expected to decline?
clarifying_info.a: Expect a drop in revenues of 100 million euros.

clarifying_info.q: What is OncoCo's current business model?
clarifying_info.a: OncoCo's income stems from one drug to treat a very niche, late-stage cancer.

clarifying_info.q: What is the price (treatment cost) per year for OncoCo's current drug?
What is the acquisition price of the liquid morphine commercial rights?
clarifying_info.a: The acquisition price is not relevant for this case.

exhibits.title: OncoCo Profit Analysis 2018-2022
exhibits.shows: A bar and line chart showing OncoCo's revenue and total costs from 2018 to 2022 (2021-2022 are forecast), along with the EBITDA margin as a line. Volume figures in thousands are also provided for each year.

exhibits.title: Morphine Market Analysis 2020
exhibits.shows: Two pie/donut charts: one showing the morphine market by formulation (in % of sales), and one showing the liquid morphine market share by product (in % of sales).

exhibits.title: Profit Analysis of Target Asset 2016-2022
exhibits.shows: A bar and line chart showing the target asset's revenue and total costs from 2016 to 2022 (2021-2022 are forecast), along with volume figures in thousands for each year.

framework: Why is OncoCo's profit expected to decline? (Profitability analysis of current business)
Should the PE fund acquire the commercial rights of liquid morphine? (M&A analysis)
- Financial attractiveness: Can the acquisition achieve >20% EBITDA margin?
- Total yearly revenue of the target asset
- Total yearly costs of the target asset
- Strategic fit: Is liquid morphine a reasonable addition to OncoCo's portfolio?
- Operational capacity and capability: Can OncoCo produce and sell the new drug?
- Risk assessment: Can OncoCo mitigate potential risks?
- Alternatives: Are there less risky opportunities to pursue?

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, why is OncoCo's profit expected to decline, and what is the magnitude of the impact?
questions.guidance: A good candidate identifies: (1) expected revenue drop of 100M EUR in 2022 (loss of 2/3 of revenues), (2) price per treatment of 10,000 EUR implied by volume data, (3) 2020 profit of 40M EUR. A very good candidate also notes: EBITDA margin in 2020 and 2021 is very high (26.7%), but drops to 0% in 2022 (revenue equals cost at 50M EUR). Should identify patent expiration and entry of generics as the root cause of the revenue decline (not merely 'competition' or 'price drop'). Should suggest transitioning to investigation of the acquisition.

math.setup: 2020: Revenue = 150M EUR, Costs = 110M EUR, EBITDA = 40M EUR. EBITDA margin = 40/150. Volume = 15K units, so price per unit = 150M / 15,000 = 10,000 EUR. 2022: Revenue = 50M EUR, Costs = 50M EUR, EBITDA = 0M EUR.
steps: Price per treatment = 150M EUR / 15,000 units = 10,000 EUR
math.answer: OncoCo faces a 100M EUR revenue drop (2/3 of revenues) in 2022 due to patent expiration and generic entry, wiping out its 40M EUR profit and driving EBITDA margin from 26.7% to 0%.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, assess the financial attractiveness of the liquid morphine market and the target asset's market position. What revenue does the target asset generate, and does it meet the PE fund's margin target?
questions.guidance: A good candidate: (1) notes that some data is missing and requests total morphine market revenue (6.25BN EUR), (2) quantifies liquid morphine as 8% of total morphine market = 500M EUR, (3) identifies target asset as category leader with 25% share of liquid morphine market = 125M EUR revenue. A very good candidate: (4) asks for the average industry EBITDA margin (20%), (5) calculates target asset profit at the 20% margin = 125M x 0.20 = 25M EUR, (6) highlights this is 15M EUR less than OncoCo's current 40M EUR profit. An outstanding candidate calculates the market share required to achieve 40M EUR profit: required revenue = 40M / 0.20 = 200M EUR; current revenue = 125M EUR; needed additional revenue = 75M EUR; additional market share = 75M / 500M = 15%; required total share = 40%. Then assesses feasibility: growing from 25% to 40% is possible given category leadership and fragmented 'Others' segment (55%).

math.setup: Total morphine market = 6.25BN EUR. Liquid morphine share = 8%. Target asset market share in liquid = 25%. Industry EBITDA margin = 20%.
steps: Target asset profit at 20% margin = 125M x 0.20 = 25M EUR
Gap vs. current OncoCo profit = 40M - 25M = 15M EUR shortfall
math.answer: Target asset revenue = 125M EUR; profit at 20% margin = 25M EUR (meets PE target of >20% EBITDA but 15M EUR below current OncoCo profit). To match current profit, OncoCo would need to grow market share from 25% to 40%, which is plausible given the fragmented 'Others' segment.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, analyze the target asset's profit history and current financial performance. What is its EBITDA margin, and what explains the dip in 2018-2019?
questions.guidance: A good candidate: (1) notes profit declined post-2017 but has recovered to previous levels by 2020, (2) calculates the price per unit carefully noting volumes are in absolute thousands (not thousands of thousands), giving 10 EUR per unit (not 10,000 EUR). A very good candidate: (3) explains the revenue decline and cost increase as the opioid crisis - physicians reduced morphine prescriptions (revenues down) and manufacturers had to settle lawsuits (costs up); morphine recovered as a basic medicine but manufacturers face tighter guidelines (fixed costs remained elevated), (4) recognizes this is a mass-market product requiring a fundamentally different business model from OncoCo's niche specialty drug, (5) calculates 2020 EBITDA margin as 32%, noting it exceeds both market average (20%) and PE target (>20%), potentially due to originator premium or economies of scale, (6) suggests assessing qualitative aspects of the acquisition before deciding.

math.setup: 2020: Revenue = 125M EUR, Total Costs = 85M EUR. Volume = 12,500 (in K = 12,500,000 units).
steps: Price per unit = 125M EUR / 12,500,000 units = 10 EUR per unit (NOT 10,000 EUR - volumes are in absolute thousands)
math.answer: Target asset EBITDA margin = 32%, above PE target and market average. Revenue dip in 2018-2019 was caused by the opioid crisis (lower prescriptions + legal settlement costs). Price = 10 EUR/unit, a mass-market product fundamentally different from OncoCo's 10,000 EUR/year specialty oncology drug.

brainstorming.prompt: What other aspects beyond EBITDA margin should the PE fund consider before acquiring the commercial rights of liquid morphine?

categories.name: Strategic
ideas: Is pain medicine a strategically reasonable addition to the oncology portfolio? Pro: diversification. Con: entirely different business model and therapeutic area.

Does OncoCo want to be associated with opioids and their negative reputation? Pro: morphine has a relatively strong reputation among opioids. Con: association could harm OncoCo's enterprise value and existing product.
Switch from a specialized product serving few patients to a mass product serving many patients. Pro: enters a larger market. Con: management may lack the expertise to compete in a mass market.

categories.name: Operational
ideas: Is OncoCo able to serve a mass market? Pro: liquid morphine is a relatively simple product not requiring extensive marketing. Con: likely needs to build production facilities and sales team from scratch.
Are there any synergies in OncoCo's production facility? Pro: lots of spare capacity starting in 2022. Con: totally different production process and scale.

categories.name: Other opportunities
ideas: Lawsuit to extend the patent of the current oncology drug. Pro: can be outsourced and requires little extra effort. Con: high uncertainty and long timeline.
Change drug formulation to extend patent for another 5-10 years. Pro: could protect revenue. Con: likely too late as R&D must be initiated now.
Acquire a different asset with better strategic fit. Pro: identify an asset more similar to OncoCo's existing business. Con: full assessment process must be repeated.

recommendation: OncoCo's board expects a 2/3 drop in revenues due to patent expiration of its only product, and suggests acquiring the commercial rights of liquid morphine to cushion the profit decline.
Despite the attractive EBITDA margin of 32% for the target asset, we do not recommend proceeding with the acquisition because the risks outweigh the potential financial benefits.
risks: OncoCo's current business model (niche specialty oncology drug, 10,000 EUR/patient/year) is in stark contrast to liquid morphine's mass-market model (10 EUR/unit), requiring heavy investment in production facilities and a new sales team.
The negative reputation of opioids could harm OncoCo's enterprise value and its existing oncology brand in the long term.
Even at the current 25% market share, the acquisition only generates 25M EUR profit vs. OncoCo's current 40M EUR, requiring a 40% market share to match current profitability.
next_steps: Look for an alternative acquisition target that fits better with OncoCo's current portfolio and business model, preferably within the same therapeutic area (Oncology).
Evaluate whether a patent extension lawsuit or formulation change for the existing drug is viable to preserve current revenue streams.
